title: Encapsulation and tunnels: GRE and IP-in-IP

videos.script: A company has two offices. Each has its own network, and each network uses private addresses, the kind that start with 192.168. {{offices}} The internet between them will not carry those addresses. Ask it to, and the packet goes nowhere. {{nowhere}} A tunnel solves that with one idea. Take the packet you cannot send, and put it inside one you can. {{inside}} The outer packet goes from one office's public address to the other's. When it arrives, the router there takes off the outer header, and the original packet carries on as if the two offices were next door. {{unwrap}} In this lesson you will build two tunnels by hand, IP-in-IP and GRE. You will watch them on the wire from the ISP's side, where both headers are visible. {{wire}} You will see what the extra header costs: bytes, and a smaller packet size that breaks things when nobody accounts for it. {{mtu}} And you will see what a tunnel does not do. Everything inside it is readable by anyone on the path. That is what lesson 2 is for. {{plain}}
